purpose: Develop a velocity-blind, formula-independent registration from raw THINGS H I intensity and SINGS 3.6 micron light into common face-on gas, stellar, and total-baryon maps.
permittedInputs: THINGS natural-weighted moment 0 image and FITS header
SINGS IRAC channel-1 image, weight image, and FITS headers
SPARC sky coordinate, distance, inclination, H I mass, 3.6 micron luminosity, effective radius, and Hubble type
forbiddenInputs: SPARC observed rotation speeds or errors
any gravity-formula prediction, score, or parameter

processing.skyCenter: fixed SPARC catalog coordinate; record photometric centroid offset but do not recenter per target velocity
processing.positionAngle: infer from robust second moments of background-subtracted SINGS 3.6 micron light inside five SPARC effective radii; never use moment 1
processing.inclination: fixed SPARC published inclination with later declared sensitivity perturbations
processing.iracBackground: weighted robust median in the outer source image, beyond max(1.2 HI radii, 6 effective radii) when covered; otherwise use the outer 15 percent image border
processing.foregroundSuppression: universal positive compact-residual replacement at 12 robust MAD above a Gaussian-smoothed image; protect the central 0.2 effective radii
processing.negativeIntensityPolicy: set negative background-subtracted light and H I intensity to zero after retaining the masks
processing.gasMassCalibration: normalize the registered H I morphology to 1.36 times the published SPARC H I mass; 1.36 is a universal helium correction
processing.stellarMassCalibration: normalize the registered 3.6 micron morphology to the published SPARC luminosity times one universal stellar mass-to-light ratio of 0.5 solar units
processing.commonResolution: Gaussian-match the stellar map to the THINGS geometric-mean beam after face-on resampling; record the approximation
processing.faceOnTransform: tangent-plane sky offsets are rotated by the image-only position angle and the minor axis is expanded by 1/cos(inclination)
processing.extent: 1.20 times the larger of the registered 99.5-percent H I radius and six SPARC effective radii
processing.interpolation: bilinear with an explicit finite-footprint map

claimBoundary: P0739 is development-only registration and may not score or rank gravity formulas.
Published per-galaxy gas mass, luminosity, distance, inclination, and sky position are baryonic or observational inputs, not gravity parameters.
The stellar mass-to-light ratio and helium factor are one universal setting shared by every galaxy.
An image-derived face-on map is not a unique three-dimensional reconstruction.
Passing registration gates cannot validate a gravity theory; it only makes the later velocity holdout interpretable.
